The Missile Defense Agency has awarded Lockheed Martin a $211.4 million contract modification to build new Configuration 3 (C3) THAAD launchers for the United Arab Emirates (UAE) under a Foreign Military Sales (FMS) agreement.
The move is intended to strengthen the UAE’s ballistic missile defense capability while allowing its THAAD launchers to be more widely dispersed across the country.
The significance of Configuration 3 goes beyond simply adding more launchers. It is part of THAAD’s broader hardware and software modernization, bringing improvements to cybersecurity and Link 16 communications while enhancing the system’s ability to integrate with a wider range of sensors.
This is particularly important for the UAE, where key targets, including air bases, ports, population centers, energy facilities, and logistics infrastructure, are spread across a relatively large area. Recent regional missile attacks have demonstrated that effective interception is only part of the equation. Maintaining sufficient interceptor reserves and the ability to sustain defensive operations through multiple attack waves are equally critical.
With the growing threat from ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones across the Middle East, the UAE is moving toward a more dispersed, interconnected, and resilient air defense architecture.

Iranian Shahed-136 loitering munitions have been spotted flying over Erbil in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region.
Several explosions were reported near Erbil International Airport and Harir Air Base.

German defense company Rheinmetall has successfully tested its FV-014 loitering munition from its new Containerized Missile Launcher.
The truck-mounted system can carry and launch up to 18 drones, including while on the move.

Lockheed Martin has conducted the first live-fire tests of its Kodiak containerized launcher, which can accommodate 12 guided rockets from the GMLRS family, as well as other MFOM (MLRS Family of Munitions) weapons used by the M270A2 MLRS and M142 HIMARS systems, including ATACMS and PrSM.
The initial tests involved launching Reduced-Range Practice Rocket (RRPR) at the Yakima Training Center in Washington state.
The Kodiak launcher is built in the form factor of a standard shipping container and, according to Lockheed Martin, “can be deployed on air, ground, or maritime platforms.”

The UAE has released several billion dollars’ worth of Iranian assets frozen in UAE banks, including 2 tonnes of gold valued at approximately $283 million.
The assets were transported to Iran aboard a Boeing 737-7KK (Reg. A6-RJA) operated by UAE-based RoyalJet. The aircraft flew from Abu Dhabi to Tehran’s Mehrabad Airport and Karaj’s Payam International Airport on August 11 and 12, with each flight lasting around one hour before returning to the UAE.
On June 8, the same aircraft flew from Abu Dhabi to Mehrabad, transporting $3 billion worth of gold.
